rows.Finding / value: Jyotiraditya Madhavrao Scindia; institutional records also use Jyotiraditya M. Scindia. Born 1 January 1971 in Mumbai.
BJP Lok Sabha member elected from Guna in 2024; Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region. NEC roster also lists him as vice-chairman.
Educated at Doon, Harvard and Stanford; BA and MBA. Entered Congress in December 2001 after his father Madhavrao’s death, with national party sponsorship and a family constituency connection.
Congress from December 2001 to March 2020; joined BJP on 11 March 2020. His ministerial career crosses Congress-led UPA and BJP-led governments.

Guna is his recurring Lok Sabha constituency; Gwalior–Chambal is a wider arena of reported political influence. Neither family association nor regional campaign activity means every local result is his personal result.
Progressed from family succession into Parliament and junior economic ministries; the 2019 defeat preceded a party switch, Rajya Sabha return and Cabinet roles, followed by the 2024 Guna comeback.
Seven contests: six direct Lok Sabha elections, with five wins and one loss, plus the successful indirect Rajya Sabha election in 2020. Assembly-party and supporter results are treated separately.

Postal modernisation, grid integration, aviation digitisation, steel incentives and telecom deployment show administrative activity across portfolios. Independent evidence of his separate contribution to durable outcomes is limited.
The 2020 break and allied MLA departures preceded the collapse of Kamal Nath’s government. Scindia framed his move as a response to Congress failures; opponents saw betrayal.

Digi Yatra enrolment complaints and the short-lived mandatory Sanchar Saathi installation policy exposed tensions between service digitisation and user choice. The later mandate was withdrawn in December 2025.
His public advocacy for women in aviation is documented. It does not establish a career-wide gender-equality record or demonstrate that representation targets were achieved.

A case of dynastic entry, national-party realignment and ministerial continuity across governments. Electoral recovery is documented; explanations based only on charisma, family or ideology remain insufficient.
4 October 2026. Current office rosters were inspected; each legal or administrative status retains its own evidence date. No later court disposition is inferred from an unsuccessful search.

rows.Description: Born in Mumbai; family background is politically relevant to later entry.
Admitted by Sonia Gandhi after his father’s death; Guna succession anticipated.
Won the Guna by-election as a Congress candidate.
Retained Guna for Congress.
Became Minister of State for Communications and Information Technology.
Won Guna again and entered the Commerce and Industry ministry as Minister of State.
Moved to Power as Minister of State with independent charge.
Southern integration completed during his Power tenure; the network had developed over decades.
Retained Guna and became Congress chief whip in Lok Sabha.
Named Congress general secretary for western Uttar Pradesh.
Lost to BJP’s Krishna Pal Singh, commonly identified as Dr K.P. Yadav.
Backed integration while qualifying that constitutional process should have been followed.
Public Congress resignation on 10 March was followed by formal BJP joining the next day.

rows.Assessment: Family succession eased entry, yet 2019 defeat and 2024 recovery show that the seat was electorally contestable. Evidence does not identify the separate effects of surname, party and personal work.

The 2020 switch was connected to a change of government in Madhya Pradesh and his return to national office. His welfare-based account and opponents’ betrayal criticism remain competing interpretations.
Service modernisation and infrastructure recur in his portfolios. Institutional biographies offer a favourable account, while shared authorship and limited evaluation constrain personal credit.
New routes and digitised services coexisted with audited sustainability problems and consent complaints. A balanced record requires both implementation measures and consequences for users.
The Sanchar Saathi reversal is a documented policy correction following criticism. It does not by itself settle whether the app’s remaining operation protects privacy adequately.
Advocacy for women pilots is part of the record; no independent longitudinal evaluation here links his interventions to recruitment, retention or leadership gains.
DoNER investment interest and reported grounding are early-stage indicators. Lasting employment, ecological effects and distribution across states remain open evaluation questions.
